facts.rubric: Located GRANT-SSO-APP using immutable identifiers and preserved effective revision v1: username m.arendse resolves to ID-40211 and open ticket SR-61203 under alert AL-88811 (rule RUL-IMPTRAV-4 v4, enabled); the similarly named m.arendse-ext (SR-61188, closed) is a different identity and AL-88802 is a suppressed duplicate from the retired v3 rule.

facts.rubric: Used the independently confirmed 2026-06-15 expedited readiness input for expedite_vendor_invalidation, then separately derived its 2026-06-17 operating outcome under containment readiness versus the non-displacing responder window calendar instead of treating a vendor promise as authorization or a completion date.
facts.statement: Halyard's confirmed standard and expedited invalidation-job dates on IR-88214: Halyard IR-88214 confirms the standard invalidation job 2026-06-16 and expedited 2026-06-12 (+USD 240); the register reflects it the next business day after verification; a vendor confirmation alone proves neither eligibility nor approval.

facts.rubric: Applied regular responder windows that do not displace protected major-incident or regulator blocks to derive the three option outcomes without using protected or blocked windows.
facts.statement: regular responder windows that do not displace protected major-incident or regulator blocks: the window calendar's first free window on or after 2026-06-17 is RESP-2 PM on 2026-06-17; RESP-1 AM on 2026-06-15 is the protected major-incident bridge and cannot be displaced; protected and blocked windows cannot be displaced.

facts.rubric: Applied AP-SO-0101 only to standard_invalidation_plan and GRANT-SSO-APP; kept tenant_wide_signout_out_of_hours outside current authority.
facts.statement: AP-SO-0101 covers one Halyard invalidation up to 6 objects with an expedite fee up to USD 250; out-of-hours responder blocks need the on-call lead and a tenant-wide sign-out needs the CISO. The approval does not select an option in advance and does not authorize tenant_wide_signout_out_of_hours.

facts.rubric: Compared all three alternatives and selected standard_invalidation_plan: it is the best currently authorized response that satisfies containment readiness versus the non-displacing responder window calendar.
facts.statement: GRC needs one defensible containment date before the 2026-06-18 regulator session; a faster or broader action has value only if it remains inside containment readiness versus the non-displacing responder window calendar.

options.consequence: standard invalidation plan revokes only tenant-revocable grants plus the standard Halyard invalidation job, lands the owner review on the first non-displacing responder window on 2026-06-17, one day before the regulator session, at no incremental cost.
options.label: standard_invalidation_plan: outcome 2026-06-17, incremental cost USD 0, SUPPORTED_AND_APPROVED

options.consequence: expedite vendor invalidation would have the federated tokens invalidated by 2026-06-15 and adds USD 240, but the first non-displacing responder window is still 2026-06-17, so it saves 0 days.
options.label: expedite_vendor_invalidation: outcome 2026-06-17, incremental cost USD 240, FEASIBLE_WITH_INFERIOR_TRADEOFF

options.consequence: tenant-wide sign-out out of hours would close the case 1 day earlier than standard invalidation plan and adds USD 620 of overtime staffing, but a tenant-wide sign-out needs the CISO and out-of-hours responder blocks need the on-call lead, neither of which AP-SO-0101 carries.
options.label: tenant_wide_signout_out_of_hours: outcome 2026-06-16, incremental cost USD 620, SEPARATE_APPROVAL_OR_POLICY_EXCEPTION_REQUIRED
